title: Callable Strategy
statement: Implement `solve(style, message)`. `style` is `upper` or `prefix`. Apply that strategy to `message`. `upper` returns the uppercase message. `prefix` returns `note:` plus the message. The caller selects the callable. You dispatch through a dict of functions.
hints: Map the style name to a function.
Call that function with the message.
Do not if/elif on the style inside the transformation itself.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: A strategy can be a function.

editorial: A strategy can be a function. You do not need a class when the behavior is one call with no stored state. The dict is the selection. The functions are the strategies. The message is the argument they share.
